title: Unused Cover from an Earlier Ostomy Supply Program Convex Barrier Notice
content:
Earlier cover still unused is deducted from the units a new Ostomy Supply Program liability notice for convex barriers (A4407) covers, according to how recent the customer's latest earlier liability notice for the convex barrier is.

## The rule

Signed fewer than 12 whole calendar months ago, the deduction is that notice's units less the barriers shipped above the allowance in the last 12 months; signed 12 to 23 whole calendar months ago, its units less the barriers shipped above the allowance in the last 24 months; otherwise nothing is deducted; the deduction is never below zero.

**Barriers shipped above the allowance in a window** are the convex-barrier refill units shipped in it less the tier's allowance times their supply days divided by 30. The tier's allowance for the convex barrier is 20 billing units per 30 days on the Ostomy Self-Pay Program, Ostomy Commercial PPO Program, Ostomy Medicare Advantage Program and Ostomy Original Medicare Program, 15 on the Ostomy Commercial HMO Program and 10 on the Ostomy Medicaid Program. A refill is in a window of N months when fewer than N whole calendar months separate its ship date from today.

| Latest earlier notice for the convex barrier signed | Deduction |
|---|---|
| Fewer than 12 whole calendar months ago | Its units less the barriers shipped above the allowance in the last 12 months, never below zero |
| 12 to 23 whole calendar months ago | Its units less the barriers shipped above the allowance in the last 24 months, never below zero |
| 24 or more months ago, or no earlier notice | Nothing |

## Worked case (hypothetical, allowance 20)

An earlier notice for 30 units signed 8 months ago. In the last 12 months the program shipped convex-barrier refills of 70 and 65 units, each for 90 days. Above the allowance: 135 less 20 multiplied by 180 divided by 30 (that is 120), so 15. The deduction is 30 less 15, that is 15. Had 160 units shipped in those refills, 40 would be above the allowance and the deduction would be zero.
